To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The genome of gill associated virus, an invertebrate virus, contains an ORF3 gene encoding a spike protein and an ORF2 gene encoding a nucleocapsid protein.

the gill-associated virus, a novel invertebrate nidivirus, has a genome organization that is unique among nidovirus species in that the spike glycoprotein ORF is downstream of the gene encoding the nucleocapsid protein.

we have completed the sequence of the gill-associated virus (+) ssRNA 3′-terminal end and that the gene organisation of this nidovirus is unique in that the putative membrane protein gene is downstream of a structural nucleocapsid protein gene and that there is no gene encoding a membrane protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genes of the nidovirus, gill-associated virus, of Penaeus monodon.
the molecular biology of the gill-associated virus, an invertebrate member of the Nidovirales order, which infects the gill epithelium and haemocytes of the giant tiger prawn, Penaeus mondon.
the molecular characterisation of the gill-associated virus, an invertebrate virus that belongs to the Nidovirales, a recently described order of viruses with a large, (+) ssRNA, segmented genomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genome organisation of GAV is unique among nidovirus genomes and that GAV is the first invertebrate nidavirus to be completely sequenced.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined the complete genome sequence of GAVE, a nidovirus of invertebrates, and that it is unique among nidovirus genomes in having no discrete membrane protein and in having the putative structural protein ORF2 gene upstream of the spike glycoprotein ORF3 gene.
we have completed the genome sequence of a nidovirus that is associated with a disease of invertebrates and that the gene organisation of this virus is unique among nidoviral genomes.
GAV is a nidovirus with a gene organisation distinct from all other known nidoviruses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GAV genome is the first to show that nidoviruses can have an ORF3 gene located downstream of the structural genes.
we now have a full genome sequence of GIV.
we have identified an invertebrate virus with a genome structure that is distinct from that of any other nidovirus and we have shown that this virus has a gene order similar to that of coronaviruses.
